defaults.tagline: Tax prep and advances, without the fluorescent rush.
defaults.heroSubtext: Same-week refund advances, year-round filing, and a studio that treats April like a conversation — not a queue.
defaults.aboutTitle: A quieter room for a loud tax season
defaults.about:
Aureum is a tax studio for people who want the advance, the filing, and a plan — without the storefront noise. We prepare individual and business returns, arrange Holiday and Shield advances when they fit, and stay on the file if a notice arrives.

You sit with one advisor. Documents are reviewed before anyone talks numbers. If an advance is not the right move, we say so.
defaults.missionStatement: Accuracy first. Advances only when they serve you. The year after April matters as much as the week of it.
defaults.servicesSectionSubtitle: Preparation, capital when you need it, and a bench for the business behind the return.

services.title: Tax prep & refund advances
services.description: A complete return, then a Holiday or Shield advance when the file supports it — often the same week.

services.title: Referrals, quietly rewarded
services.description: Send someone you trust. When they file, you receive the season’s bonus. No scripts, no pressure.

services.title: Business tax & audit care
services.description: Schedule C and 1120 work, plus representation if the IRS writes. Existing clients are not billed for audit support.

steps.title: Bring the file
steps.description: ID, SSN, W-2s or pay stubs, and dependent documents. We send a short list before you arrive.

steps.title: Sit with an advisor
steps.description: One person reviews the year with you. No rotating seasonal desk.

steps.title: Choose the advance
steps.description: If an advance fits, we walk the fees and the timeline. You can always wait for the IRS.

steps.title: File, then stay in touch
steps.description: The return goes out. Quarterly notes follow so next April is quieter than this one.

faqs.question: Do I have to take an advance?
faqs.answer: No. Many clients file and wait for the IRS. We only size an advance after the return is complete, and you can decline it.

faqs.question: How fast can funds arrive?
faqs.answer: When the file is clean, Holiday and Shield advances often fund the same week — sometimes the same day.

faqs.question: What should I bring?
faqs.answer: Photo ID, Social Security numbers, W-2s or pay stubs, and documents for anyone you claim. We send a checklist when you book.

faqs.question: Do you handle business returns?
faqs.answer: Yes. Sole proprietors and corporations, plus audit support. Existing clients are not charged if the IRS writes.

blogPosts.title: An advance is not the refund
blogPosts.excerpt: Why we size funds after the return, and why taking less is sometimes the better year.
blogPosts.body:
An advance is a short loan against a finished return. It is repaid when the IRS pays. Fees, if any, come out of that refund.

We do not quote a number until the file is done. That is how you avoid taking more than the year can carry.
blogPosts.author: Elena Voss

blogPosts.title: What we ask you to bring
blogPosts.excerpt: A short list that keeps the sitting to one visit.
blogPosts.body:
Photo ID. Social Security numbers. W-2s or pay stubs. Birth certificates for dependents, plus proof they lived with you.

If something is missing we will say so before we start, not after you have already sat down.
